comment: PlantMind V1 demonstration knowledge base. Relationships are illustrative for the prototype and are NOT scientifically exhaustive.

entities.name: Tomato
entities.description: Warm-season fruiting crop (Solanum lycopersicum). Susceptible to several fungal and oomycete foliar diseases, especially in humid conditions.

entities.name: Rose
entities.description: Ornamental flowering shrub (Rosa spp.). Commonly affected by fungal leaf diseases and powdery mildew.

entities.name: Potato
entities.description: Tuber crop (Solanum tuberosum). Highly susceptible to late blight under cool, wet conditions.

entities.name: Apple
entities.description: Fruit tree (Malus domestica). Prone to fungal leaf diseases and powdery mildew in humid climates.

entities.name: Early Blight
entities.description: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. Produces dark brown spots with concentric rings, often surrounded by yellowing tissue, starting on lower leaves.

entities.name: Late Blight
entities.description: Aggressive oomycete disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. Produces water-soaked dark lesions that spread rapidly in cool, humid weather.

entities.name: Powdery Mildew
entities.description: Fungal disease producing white, powdery patches on leaf surfaces. Favored by humidity with poor air circulation.

entities.name: Leaf Spot
entities.description: General fungal leaf-spotting condition producing discrete brown or black spots, sometimes with yellow halos.

entities.name: Nitrogen Deficiency
entities.description: Nutrient disorder causing uniform yellowing, typically starting with older, lower leaves and reduced growth.

entities.name: Overwatering Stress
entities.description: Physiological stress caused by waterlogged roots: yellowing leaves, wilting despite moist soil, and general decline.

entities.name: Yellow Leaves
entities.description: Chlorosis: leaf tissue turning yellow. Can indicate nutrient deficiency, overwatering, or disease.

entities.name: Brown Spots
entities.description: Discrete brown necrotic spots on leaves, often with concentric rings or yellow halos.

entities.name: White Powder
entities.description: White, powdery or dusty coating on leaf surfaces, typical of powdery mildew.

entities.name: Wilting
entities.description: Drooping or loss of turgor in leaves and stems despite available water.

entities.name: Leaf Curling
entities.description: Leaves curling upward, downward, or inward; can indicate stress, pest damage, or disease.

entities.name: Dark Lesions
entities.description: Dark brown to black necrotic patches on leaves or stems, often water-soaked in appearance.

entities.name: High Humidity
entities.description: Sustained high relative humidity around foliage, which favors fungal and oomycete disease development.

entities.name: Low Light
entities.description: Insufficient light exposure, weakening plants and prolonging leaf wetness.

entities.name: Excess Moisture
entities.description: Overly wet growing medium or persistently damp foliage.

entities.name: Poor Ventilation
entities.description: Stagnant air around plants, which raises local humidity and favors fungal spores.

entities.name: Nutrient Deficiency
entities.description: Insufficient nutrient availability in the growing medium.

entities.name: Adequate Light
entities.description: Appropriate light exposure for healthy photosynthesis and sturdy growth.

entities.name: Improve Ventilation
entities.description: Increase air circulation around plants by spacing, pruning, or using fans. Reduces humidity and fungal pressure.

entities.name: Reduce Excess Watering
entities.description: Water only when the topsoil begins to dry; water the base rather than the foliage.

entities.name: Remove Affected Leaves
entities.description: Prune and dispose of diseased leaves to reduce inoculum and slow disease spread.

entities.name: Improve Light
entities.description: Relocate the plant or supplement lighting so it receives adequate, appropriate light.

entities.name: Nutrient Management
entities.description: Apply a balanced fertilizer at the correct rate and interval to correct deficiencies.

entities.name: Monitor Disease Progression
entities.description: Inspect the plant regularly, photograph symptoms, and track whether the condition is improving or worsening.
